Hence, the Ritz projection $R_h$ introduced in \eqref{eq:def_ritz_projection} is well defined for any $\psi \in H^2_0(\Om)\cap H^{\frac52-\varepsilon}(\Om)$.

issues.failure_explanation: With $\theta=\frac12-\varepsilon$ fixed in the same paragraph, Assumption 2 defines $X=\mathcal A^{-1}(H^{-1-\theta})=\mathcal A^{-1}(H^{-3/2+\varepsilon})$. Since the clamped biharmonic operator shifts Sobolev regularity by 4 (cf. the paper's own Proposition: $H^{-1}$ data yield $H^3$ solutions), $X$ is the $H^{5/2+\varepsilon}$-scale, exactly as stated in the Remark. The Section 3.2.2 claim $X=H^2_0\cap H^{5/2-\varepsilon}$ is therefore false (e.g. $\psi=\mathcal A^{-1}g$ with $g\in H^{-3/2-\varepsilon}\setminus H^{-3/2+\varepsilon}$ lies in $H^2_0\cap H^{5/2-\varepsilon}$ but not in $X$), so the paper contains two contradictory characterizations of $X$. Consequently, the follow-up claim that $R_h$ is well defined for every $\psi\in H^2_0\cap H^{5/2-\varepsilon}$ overstates the domain of the Ritz projection: for such $\psi$ outside $X$, the interior-penalty bilinear form's edge terms (traces of second derivatives, which require more than $H^{5/2}$-regularity) are not well defined.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the exponent in both sentences of Section 3.2.2 to $H^{\frac52+\varepsilon}$, making them consistent with Assumption 2's definition $X=\mathcal A^{-1}(H^{-1-\theta})$, $\theta=\frac12-\varepsilon$, and with the Remark.
issues.overall_effect: The scope of Assumption 2's space $X$ and of the Ritz projection for the $C^0$ interior penalty method is misstated (by $2\varepsilon$ in the Sobolev exponent); a reader could wrongly assume the framework (Ritz projection, Galerkin orthogonality) applies to stream functions with only $H^{5/2-\varepsilon}$ regularity, for which the discrete bilinear form's consistency is not available. No labelled formal result relies on the false version: the convergence theorem only needs $\psi\in L^2(H^3)\subset X$ on convex domains, and the main theorem uses $X$ only through Assumption 2's definition.
issues.title: False characterization of the space $X$ for the $C^0$ interior penalty method ($H^{5/2-\varepsilon}$ instead of $H^{5/2+\varepsilon}$), overstating the domain of the Ritz projection
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the exponent sign restores internal consistency; all formal results, rates, and the advertised scope (natural data on convex domains give $\psi\in L^2(H^3)\subset X$) survive unchanged, and no new argument is needed.
